worked: Single, age 61. Born 1964-01-02: 61 at December 31, 2025. The form's exemption needs 62 by December 31, so the taxable benefits stay in income (they would be exempt only as disability benefits, which the projection cannot see). Federal taxable Social Security: other income 40,000.00 + half of benefits 15,000.00 = provisional 55,000.00; 85% x (55,000.00 - 34,000.00) + 4,500.00 = 22,350.00. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 40,000.00 + taxable Social Security 22,350.00 = 62,350.00. Federal taxable income = 62,350.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 46,600.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form MO-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 62,350.00. Line 2 additions 0.00. Line 3 total income 62,350.00. Line 4 subtractions 0.00. Line 6 Missouri adjusted gross income 62,350.00 - 0.00 = 62,350.00. MO-A Part 3 Section C (Y, age 61): Line 1 22,350.00; Line 3 0.00 (under 62 at December 31, no exemption; the benefit stays taxed). Section C Line 4 total 0.00. Form MO-1040 Line 8 pension and Social Security exemption 0.00. Lines 9-13 federal income tax deduction not applied (not modelled; the household's federal tax is not an input). Line 14 standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 26 subtotal 62,350.00 - 0.00 - 15,750.00 = 46,600.00. Line 29 taxable income 46,600.00. Tax by the bands (0% to 1,313): 2% x 1,313.00 = 26.26 + 2.5% x 1,313.00 = 32.825 + 3% x 1,313.00 = 39.39 + 3.5% x 1,313.00 = 45.955 + 4% x 1,313.00 = 52.52 + 4.5% x 1,313.00 = 59.085 + 4.7% x 37,409.00 = 1758.223; total 2014.258 = 2,014.26. The chart and Tax Calculation Worksheet (instructions p21) round to the dollar and give 2014; expected keeps the bands. state_agi (after every relief, as the check format defines it) = Line 6 62,350.00 - Line 8 0.00 = 62,350.00; the form's Missouri AGI is Line 6, 62,350.00.
accepted_approximations: The chart's cumulative amounts are rounded to whole dollars and the tax to the nearest dollar; the bands here do neither.
The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).
